title: Study notes
html:
Anatomy that gets asked

Retroperitoneal: kidneys, ureters, adrenals, pancreas (except tail tip), duodenum 2–4, ascending and descending colon, aorta, IVC and lymph nodes. Intraperitoneal: stomach, spleen, liver, transverse and sigmoid colon, jejunum and ileum.

Lymph nodes

Pathological if short axis > 10 mm (retrocrural > 6 mm), round, loss of fatty hilum, necrosis. Best seen on contrast CT (separates nodes from vessels and bowel); US is limited by bowel gas.

Adrenal masses

  • US first-line, but CT is the method of choice: unenhanced < 10 HU = lipid-rich adenoma; otherwise washout CT (absolute > 60 %) or chemical-shift MRI (signal drop).
  • Myelolipoma: macroscopic fat – hyperechoic on US, NEGATIVE HU on CT (hypodense) – specific.
  • Bilateral masses → metastases (lung, breast, melanoma), hyperplasia, haemorrhage, pheochromocytoma (MEN).
  • Pheochromocytoma: enhancing, heterogeneous, T2 "light bulb", MIBG/DOTATATE – a negative US does not exclude it. Carcinoma: > 4–6 cm, necrosis, invasion.

Female pelvis

  • Transvaginal US first; MRI characterises and stages locally (T2 is the key sequence); CT/PET for distant spread.
  • Endometrium in post-menopausal bleeding > 4 mm → biopsy; endometrial cancer staged by MRI (myometrial invasion > 50 % = IB; cervical stroma = II).
  • Ovary (IOTA): benign = unilocular, smooth, < 10 cm, acoustic shadow; malignant = irregular solid parts, papillary projections, thick septa, flow, ascites. Endometrioma = "chocolate" ground-glass cyst; dermoid = fat + calcification (tooth).
  • Fibroids: well-defined hypoechoic myometrial masses, may calcify (popcorn on KUB).

Male pelvis

Prostate: mpMRI before biopsy (PI-RADS 1–5; 4–5 biopsy), 70 % of cancers in the peripheral zone, blastic bone metastases; TRUS for volume and guidance; BPH enlarges the transition zone. Testis: US + Doppler – torsion = no intratesticular flow; tumours are hypoechoic.

Exam reflexes

  • Fat in an adrenal mass = myelolipoma; fat in a renal mass = angiomyolipoma.
  • Obesity helps CT (fat outlines organs) but limits US.
  • Local staging = MRI; distant staging = CT.
